function.name: user_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a given user by their ID. It filters the mandates based on their status if provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

user_id.description: The unique identifier of the user for whom mandates are being fetched.

status.description: The status of the mandates to fetch. If not specified, mandates of all statuses are returned.

message.content: Sure! To retrieve the mandates, I’ll need the user’s unique identifier. Could you please provide the `user_id`? Once I have that, I’ll fetch both the pending and active mandates for you.
message.reasoning: The user says: "need all pending and active mandates". They want to fetch mandates for a user? But they didn't provide a user ID. The function requires user_id. We need to ask for user_id. Also maybe they want both pending and active. So we can call function with status unspecified or maybe we need to fetch all statuses? The function signature: status optional. If not specified, returns all statuses. But they specifically want pending and active. That means we could call twice: once with status="pending" and once with status="active". Or we could call once without status to get all, then filter. But the function only accepts one status. So we need to call twice. But we don't have user_id. So we should ask for user_id first.
